\medskip\par\noindent\textbf{L-LIT-FOLD}\quad(\textsc{violated})\\*[0.15em]
A literal synthesized by the enum constant folder denotes the member's runtime value.\\*[0.15em]
{\small\emph{Anchor:} \texttt{enumFold} (string-concat arms); \texttt{enumNumOrUnknown}}\par
\nopagebreak
\textsc{violated}, witnessed end-to-end (deep dive G; issue draft \path{enum-concat-imprecise-fold.md}): the string-concat arms concatenate operand \emph{lexemes}, and a direct numeric-literal operand bypasses the double-safe gate that guards numeric fold results, so a beyond-precision spelling produces a member literal whose spelling is not the runtime string (\texttt{"x" + 1e-400} folds to \texttt{"x1e-400"}; the runtime value is \texttt{"x0"}). A prerequisite of the future preservation theorem's switch-coverage lemma (semantic case coverage consumes member-value faithfulness)

\nopagebreak

\medskip\par\noindent\textbf{L-SUB-CLOSED-ABSENCE}\quad(\textsc{open})\\*[0.15em]

{\small\emph{Anchor:} \texttt{TFields::isSub\_IndexPair}; \texttt{TFields::isSub\_NamedFields} (extra-field arm); \texttt{closeObjectType}}\par
\nopagebreak
\textsc{open} (conditional): the syntactic checks are verified at every index-pair arm and at \texttt{isSub\_NamedFields}'s extra-source-field-against-target-index arm (deep dive D, the absence corollary); the containment they induce is conditional on the recursive \texttt{isSub} verdicts, exactly as the read direction is inside L-SUB

\nopagebreak
\textsc{violated}, witnessed end-to-end in both directions (deep dive C; issue draft \path{expansion-key-collision.md}): two same-named, same-argument aliases from different modules share one \texttt{ExpansionKey}, so whichever expands first is served for both — an unsound acceptance one way (a \texttt{string}-typed call returns \texttt{undefined}) and an order-dependent false rejection the other, its diagnostic anchored in the wrong module; renaming either alias restores the correct verdicts. Refutes the source comment claiming the collision could not yet be triggered (upstream \#889); fix direction: key by definition identity

\medskip\par\noindent\textbf{ACCESSOR-METHOD}\quad(\textsc{violated})\\*[0.15em]
Accessor (\texttt{get}/\texttt{set}) members must be typed as fields, not methods; today a getter is a call signature, so \texttt{c.p()} type-checks and throws.\\*[0.15em]
{\small\emph{Anchor:} \texttt{isGetSet} (parser-only); member typing}\par
\nopagebreak
\textsc{violated}, witnessed end-to-end (SKJS-specific; tsc rejects with TS6234): the parser's \texttt{isGetSet} marker is never read by the checker, so a getter \texttt{get p(): T} is typed as a method \texttt{p(): T}. \texttt{c.p()} is accepted and throws at runtime (\texttt{c.p} is not a function). Issue draft \path{getter-typed-as-method.md}. Adjacent to F's accessor caveat and L-GETSET, but a distinct (member-typing) hole

\medskip\par\noindent\textbf{L-SUB-TSINST}\quad(\textsc{violated})\\*[0.15em]
The reflexive \texttt{TSInst} fast path in \texttt{isSub} (same name, arguments equal after \texttt{peekRaw}) is sound.\\*[0.15em]
{\small\emph{Anchor:} \texttt{TType::isSub} (TSInst reflexive arm)}\par
\nopagebreak
\textsc{violated} (deep dive D): the inclusion at the verdict state holds for unconstrained bindings, but the arm reads an unsealed \texttt{SVOpen} candidate via \texttt{peekRaw} without the covariant seal the slow path performs, so a later contravariant grow widens the binding and reads through aliases break — witnessed end-to-end (a value typed \texttt{number} holds a string; issue draft \path{reflexive-tsinst-fastpath-unsealed-read.md}). For constrained variables the equality claim also fails as stated: the occurrence denotes $\sem{t_2}_\rho \cap \bigcap\sem{C}$, not $\sem{t_2}_\rho$
